  Before submitting a pull request, update your branch to the latest code.

  If you have made many commits, we ask you to squash them into atomic units of work. Most of tickets should have one commit only, especially bug fixes, which makes them easier to back port.

  Push changes to your fork:

  In order to make a pull request,
  * Navigate to the OpenMRS repository you just pushed to (e.g. https://github.com/your-user-name/openmrs-core)

  * Click "Update Commit Range".
  * Ensure the changesets you introduced are included in the "Commits" tab.
  * Ensure that the "Files Changed" incorporate all of your changes.
  * Fill in some details about your potential patch including a meaningful title.
  * Click "Send pull request".

rows.title: TRUNK-6707: Cache global property lookups
rows.excerpt:
me. Results are now cached in the existing API cache manager, with unset properties stored as an explicit `ABSENT` marker.                                                                     

Evicted on save/set/update/purge through the API, and the whole API cache is cleared on context refresh, covering properties modules insert via Liquibase. Direct SQL writes to `global_property` aren't supported — they already bypass the `GlobalPropertyListener` caches today.                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                     
Tests: 6 added to `HibernateAdministrationDAOTest`, new `GlobalPropertyCacheTest` with 10 covering cache hits, negative caching and eviction on every write path, plus `CacheConfigTest`. Full `api` suite: 5181 tests, 0 failures.
